title: Feature/1986
summary: In a shared reading session you can now **follow** another person: your screen scrolls along with the exact verses they're reading, not just their chapter. A note above the reader's tools says who you're following; clicking it asks whether to stop. If you scroll well away from them, following pauses and the note offers to jump back. The host chooses who may follow whom in **Session settings** under a new **Following** section.

links.label: Issue 1986: Add the ability to automatically follow a user's place in a shared session

setup.title: Get two browsers side by side
setup.body: Every test needs two people. Use two different browsers on a computer (for example Chrome and Firefox), or one normal window and one private/incognito window (Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome/Edge, Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox; on Mac use Cmd instead of Ctrl). Below they're called the **host browser** and the **guest browser**. Place them side by side so you can watch both at once.

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Open the preview link at the top of this page in both browsers. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like an older version of Seed Bible, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac). Always start from this exact link, not the main Seed Bible site.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in in the host browser. Seed Bible emails you a code to type in. If the guest browser asks you to sign in to join, use a **different** email address there.

setup.title: Start a shared session
setup.body: In the host browser, open **John 3**. Open the tab's menu (the **⋮** / tab options button on the tab) and choose **Share session**. Copy the link it gives you and open it in the guest browser. Both browsers should now show John 3 with both people listed as participants.

setup.title: Make the guest window shorter than the host's
setup.body: Some tests need the guest to see fewer verses than the host. Make the guest browser window noticeably shorter (or zoom it in with **Ctrl +** / **Cmd +**) so it shows clearly fewer verses than the host window.

sections.title: Following someone
sections.intro: Leave **Session settings → Following** on its starting choice for this section.

tests.title: Following is on for everyone by default
tests.why: Issue 1986 asks for four choices, with "Users can follow each other" as the default.
steps: In the host browser, open the shared tab's menu and choose **Session settings**.
Scroll to the **Following** section and read the choices.
Close the dialog.
expected: A **Following** section lists four choices: **Users can follow each other**, **Users can follow only hosts**, **Users automatically follow the host**, and **Users cannot follow**.
**Users can follow each other** is selected, with the line "Anyone can follow anyone else. Nobody follows automatically." under the choices.

tests.title: A Follow button appears next to other people, not yourself
steps: In the guest browser, open the participants list: on the shared tab in the side list, choose **Show participants** (the small arrow under the tab) if the list is folded away.
Look at the row for the host and the row for yourself.
Also open the shared tab's menu and look for a **Participants** item; choose it.
expected: The host's row has a **Follow** button. Your own row does not.
The tab menu has a new **Participants** item. It opens a **Participants** window listing everyone, host first, with **Follow** on the host's row.

tests.title: Following scrolls you to the verse the other person is looking at
steps: In the host browser, scroll John 3 down so verse 16 is near the top of the screen.
In the guest browser, scroll back to the top of John 3.
In the guest browser, choose **Follow** on the host's row.
expected: The guest's reader jumps so the first verse the host can see (around verse 16) is at the top of the guest's screen.
A rounded note appears above the guest's reader tools and chapter controls, showing the host's avatar and "Following <host's name>", with a border in the host's color.
The host's **Follow** button in the guest's participants list now reads **Stop following**.

tests.title: The follower keeps up as the other person scrolls
tests.before: The guest is following the host from the previous test.
steps: In the host browser, slowly scroll down to around verse 25, then back up to around verse 5.
Watch the guest browser the whole time. Don't touch it.
expected: The guest's screen scrolls along, keeping the host's first visible verse at the top. It stays within a verse or two of the host and doesn't jump back and forth.
The note keeps saying "Following <host's name>".

tests.title: With a smaller screen you can scroll within the other person's view
tests.why: Issue 1986: when the leader sees more verses than you, you should be able to scroll inside their view without being snapped back to its top.
tests.before: The guest window is shorter than the host's, and the guest is following the host.
steps: In the host browser, scroll so verses 10 to about 20 are on screen, then stop.
In the guest browser, scroll down a little so verse 14 or 15 is at the top. Stay within the verses the host can see.
Wait 5 seconds.
In the host browser, scroll down by just one or two verses.
expected: After your small scroll, the guest stays where you put it: the screen is not pulled back up to verse 10.
The note still says "Following <host's name>" (not "stopped following").
When the host scrolls a little, the guest is not snapped back to the host's top verse while your verse is still within what the host sees.

tests.title: Following carries you to a new chapter
tests.before: The guest is following the host.
steps: In the host browser, go to the next chapter (**John 4**) and scroll so verse 7 is near the top.
expected: The guest browser moves to John 4 by itself and lands with the host's first visible verse (around verse 7) at the top.
The note still says "Following <host's name>".

tests.title: Clicking the note asks whether to stop following
tests.before: The guest is following the host.
steps: In the guest browser, click the "Following <host's name>" note.
In the window that opens, choose **Cancel**.
Click the note again and this time choose **Stop following**.
In the host browser, scroll a few verses.
expected: A window titled **Stop following?** says "You'll stop following <host's name>." with **Cancel** and **Stop following** buttons.
**Cancel** closes it and the note stays.
**Stop following** closes it and the note disappears. The host's row shows **Follow** again.
When the host scrolls, the guest's screen no longer moves.

tests.title: The Stop following button in the participants list works too
steps: In the guest browser, choose **Follow** on the host's row again.
Then choose **Stop following** on the same row.
expected: Following starts (the note appears), then stops right away with no question asked: the note disappears and the button reads **Follow**.

setup.title: Start following again
setup.body: Put both browsers on **John 3**. In the host browser, scroll so verse 10 is near the top. In the guest browser, choose **Follow** on the host's row.

tests.title: Scrolling well away from the other person pauses following
tests.why: Issue 1986 asks that scrolling far enough outside the other person's verses detaches you, and the note says "You've stopped following X. Click to resume".
steps: In the guest browser, scroll down quickly to the end of John 3 (well past anything the host can see).
Stop and wait 2 seconds.
In the host browser, scroll a few verses.
expected: The guest stays where they scrolled; they are not pulled back to the host.
The note changes to "You've stopped following <host's name>. Click to resume".
The guest's screen doesn't move when the host scrolls.

tests.title: Clicking the paused note jumps back and follows again
tests.before: The note says you've stopped following, from the previous test.
steps: In the guest browser, click the "You've stopped following …" note.
In the host browser, scroll a few verses.
expected: No question is asked. The guest jumps straight back to the host's first visible verse.
The note says "Following <host's name>" again, and the guest keeps up as the host scrolls.

tests.title: Going to another chapter yourself pauses following
tests.before: The guest is following the host.
steps: In the guest browser, use the chapter controls to go to **John 5** (or pick another chapter from the book menu).
Wait a couple of seconds, then click the note.
expected: The guest stays on John 5 and the note changes to "You've stopped following <host's name>. Click to resume".
Clicking the note takes the guest back to the host's chapter and verse, and following resumes.

tests.title: Leaving the session's tab or the other person leaving ends following
tests.before: The guest is following the host.
steps: Close the host browser completely (or close the shared tab in it).
Watch the guest browser for up to 30 seconds.
expected: Once the host is no longer listed as a participant, the note disappears from the guest browser. Nothing is left showing a person who isn't there.
Afterwards, reopen the session link in the host browser so both are back in the session for the next section.

sections.title: Host choices for following
sections.intro: The host changes the choice in **Session settings → Following**. The guest's screen should update without reloading.

tests.title: Only the host can change the following choice
steps: In the guest browser, open the participants list or tab menu and look for **Session settings**. If it's there, open it and try clicking a different choice under **Following**.
expected: The guest either has no **Session settings**, or the **Following** choices are greyed out and clicking them changes nothing.

tests.title: "Users can follow only hosts" hides Follow next to non-hosts
steps: In the host browser, open **Session settings** and choose **Users can follow only hosts**.
Read the line under the choices, then close the dialog.
In the host browser, open the participants list and look at the guest's row.
In the guest browser, open the participants list and look at the host's row.
expected: The line reads "Anyone can follow a host. Nobody follows automatically."
The host sees **no Follow** button on the guest's row, because the guest isn't a host.
The guest still sees **Follow** on the host's row, and following the host works.

tests.title: "Users cannot follow" removes Follow and ends any follow
tests.before: The guest is following the host (choose **Follow** on the host's row if not).
steps: In the host browser, open **Session settings** and choose **Users cannot follow**. Close the dialog.
Look at the guest browser's note and participants list.
expected: The line under the choices reads "Following is turned off for everyone."
In the guest browser the note disappears and nobody's row has a **Follow** button.
The host scrolling no longer moves the guest.

tests.title: "Users automatically follow the host" starts following the host
tests.why: Issue 1986: with this choice, people follow the host when they join.
steps: In the host browser, open **Session settings** and choose **Users automatically follow the host**. Close the dialog.
Watch the guest browser.
Then close the guest browser's session tab (or the whole private window) and open the session link again in a fresh guest window.
expected: The line under the choices reads "People follow the host when they join. They can still follow someone else."
Without doing anything, the guest gets the "Following <host's name>" note and starts scrolling along with the host.
After rejoining, the guest again follows the host straight away.

tests.title: Stopping on purpose isn't undone by automatic following
tests.before: The choice is still **Users automatically follow the host** and the guest is following the host.
steps: In the guest browser, click the note and choose **Stop following**.
Wait 10 seconds while the host scrolls and changes chapter.
expected: The guest stays unfollowed: the note doesn't come back on its own.

tests.title: The note fits on a phone-width screen
steps: Make the guest browser very narrow (about the width of a phone), or open the session link on a phone.
Follow the host.
Scroll a little and open and close the reader tools if your screen has them.
expected: The note sits just above the reader's bottom tools and chapter controls, stretching across the screen with small margins.
It doesn't cover the chapter controls or the tools, and the last verses of the chapter can still be scrolled above it.
A long name or the longer "You've stopped following …" text wraps inside the note instead of running off the screen.

tests.title: The note and settings are readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the guest browser to dark mode in the app's settings.
Follow the host and look at the note, then let it pause and look again.
In the host browser, switch to dark mode and open **Session settings → Following**.
expected: The note's text and avatar are easy to read against its background in both states.
The selected choice under **Following** is clearly marked in dark mode.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Without following, chapter sync works as before
steps: Make sure the guest isn't following anyone (no note on screen). Set **Following** back to **Users can follow each other**.
In the host browser, go to **John 6**.
expected: The guest moves to John 6 as it did before this change (only the chapter; their scroll position is their own).

tests.title: The participants list still offers its other actions
steps: Open the participants list in both browsers, and in the host browser also open **Session settings** and look at its participant list.
Look for the actions that were there before, such as **Add friend**, **Make co-host** (in Session settings, host only), and where people reading elsewhere are.
expected: The existing buttons and labels are still there and work; **Follow** sits alongside them without pushing anything off the row or out of view.

notCovered: Many English text entries were moved around in the app's translation file. Their wording didn't change, so nothing should look different, but a missing label anywhere would show up as a raw code like `delete-save-failed`.
Following a co-host when the choice is "Users can follow only hosts" isn't tested here; the code treats co-hosts as hosts for this.
Whether a follower's moves ever drag the rest of the session to a new chapter needs three people to check and is covered by the PR's unit tests instead.
